discussion_comments.comment_body:
`validateExtraNodeAllocatableResources` only sees the new pod, so nothing limits how this field changes after the pod binds. NodeRestriction covers the kubelet, though any other identity with `pods/status` can grow or shrink the entries on a running pod after the kubelet sized its cgroups. Quota and the scheduler then track the new values while the cgroups keep the old ones. Could we pass `oldPod` and allow changes only while `spec.nodeName` is empty (set in PreBind, cleared in Unreserve)?

Related: `validatePodLevelResourcesCoverDRA` only runs on resize. A status write that adds more than `spec.resources` covers passes here. Quota then charges the pod level value while the kubelet adds the larger amount to the pod cgroup. Running the coverage check here when the field changes would close that.

Checking. I do not see other pod status fields being validated against external actors mutating it. 
Besides, once the pod starts running, component-helpers starts using resources reported in `pod.status.resources` (read from cgroups) for calculations, so an external actor mutating extraNodeAllocatableResouces does not automatically grow/shrink the pod footprint as kubelet only configures pod cgroup at admission or during resize.

It looks like `CgroupOptions` needs to be included in the effective security-context merge.

In my test, Kubernetes stored `mountMode: Writable`, but kubelet sent the default `ReadOnly` value and containerd produced a read-only cgroup mount.

When `pod.spec.securityContext` is non-nil, `DetermineEffectiveSecurityContext` currently drops the container-level `CgroupOptions` field. 

The following addition in `DetermineEffectiveSecurityContext` in `pkg/securitycontext/util.go`  could fix the problem:
```
if containerSc.CgroupOptions != nil {
    effectiveSc.CgroupOptions = containerSc.CgroupOptions.DeepCopy()
}
```
